summary.tagline: Explore 2,000-year-old standing stones and the magnificent Five Sisters of Kintail.
summary.seo_title: Visiting Glen Shiel and Kintail Standing Stones

travel.headline: Review Scottish Trust Guidelines for Ranger-Led Activities
travel.reservation: Access to the glen and historic sites is generally open, though ranger-led activities such as guided sea kayaking or hill walking may require advance booking through the National Trust for Scotland. As specific systems can change, always check the official site for seasonal event schedules and mountain safety updates.

days.title: Ancient History and Highland Peaks
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Kyle of Lochalsh

stops.name: Cill Fhearchair
stops.detail: Visit this 2,000-year-old standing stone and burial ground located near the historic site of the Battle of Glenshiel.

days.driving: Allow for 30 to 60 minutes of travel time; conditions vary with weather and narrow roads.
days.note: Pacing is a suggestion; mountain weather can change rapidly and influence walking speeds.

intel.title: Trailhead Access
intel.text: Specific parking lot capacities for Cill Fhearchair are not detailed in official sources. Visitors should check for designated laybys or Trust-managed parking areas upon arrival.

intel.title: Connectivity Gaps
intel.text: Cellular signal strength in the deep glens and high Munros is not officially documented. Users should carry physical maps for navigation.

intel.title: Local Supplies
intel.text: Fuel availability within Glen Shiel is not stated; confirm levels in larger gateway towns before entering the glen.

intel.title: Wildlife Viewing
intel.text: Look for otters in Loch Duich and red deer on the slopes throughout the day. Golden eagles are best spotted soaring above the high ridges.

intel.title: Mountain Hazards
intel.text: The Five Sisters of Kintail offer challenging hill walking and Munro scaling. Check current weather conditions as these routes involve steep, wild terrain.

plan.arrival: Collect a rental vehicle in Inverness or Kyle of Lochalsh, securing supplies before entering the more remote glen areas.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is suitable for main roads, though RV travelers should check for passing place restrictions on narrow Highland routes.
plan.goldenHour: Views of the Five Sisters of Kintail offer a dramatic backdrop as light changes, though cloud cover is frequent.
